ai.description: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* reaches 60 mm SVL. It is pale grey-brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a white underside. Key features include keeled subdigital lamellae and a row of enlarged dorsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* is best distinguished by its lack of enlarged, keeled tubercles on the back, which are replaced by small, granular scales uniform in size.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in the Himalayan foothills, typically found at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt small insects on vertical surfaces like rock faces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, primarily from March to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus aquilonius* occurs in the northern Indian subcontinent, primarily across the Himalayan foothills and adjacent plains, ranging from lowlands up to 1,500m.
